claim: The locus coeruleus (LC) is a small bilateral nucleus located in the dorsal pons of the brainstem.
source: The LC is a small bilateral nucleus located in the dorsal pons of the brainstem, which serves as the brain's primary site for the production of the neuromodulator NE.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the anatomical location of the LC.

claim: The LC serves as the brain's primary site for the production of norepinephrine (NE).
source: The LC is a small bilateral nucleus located in the dorsal pons of the brainstem, which serves as the brain's primary site for the production of the neuromodulator NE.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the function of the LC.

claim: NE-producing neurons in the LC project widely to many regions of the central nervous system.
source: NE-producing neurons in the LC project widely to many regions of the central nervous system to modulate a variety of highly divergent functions including attention, arousal, pain, mood, and the response to stress (Poe et al., 2020; Chandler et al., 2019; Sara, 2009; Morris et al., 2020; Suárez-Pereira et al., 2022; Ross and Van Bockstaele, 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: LC-NE neurons modulate attention, arousal, pain, mood, and the response to stress.
source: NE-producing neurons in the LC project widely to many regions of the central nervous system to modulate a variety of highly divergent functions including attention, arousal, pain, mood, and the response to stress (Poe et al., 2020; Chandler et al., 2019; Sara, 2009; Morris et al., 2020; Suárez-Pereira et al., 2022; Ross and Van Bockstaele, 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The rodent LC comprises approximately 3000 NE neurons (~1500–1600 on each side of the brainstem).
source: The LC, translated as 'blue spot' (in recognition of its characteristic presence of neuromelanin pigment), comprises merely 3000 NE neurons in the rodent (~1500–1600 on each side of the brainstem) (Poe et al., 2020), and estimates in the human LC range from 19,000 to 46,000 total NE neurons (German et al., 1988).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Poe et al., 2020.

claim: Estimates of total NE neurons in the human LC range from 19,000 to 46,000.
source: The LC, translated as 'blue spot' (in recognition of its characteristic presence of neuromelanin pigment), comprises merely 3000 NE neurons in the rodent (~1500–1600 on each side of the brainstem) (Poe et al., 2020), and estimates in the human LC range from 19,000 to 46,000 total NE neurons (German et al., 1988).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to German et al., 1988.

claim: The LC-NE system is implicated in many neurodegenerative, neuropsychiatric, and neurological disorders.
source: Consistent with these roles, the LC-NE system is implicated in many neurodegenerative, neuropsychiatric, and neurological disorders (Morris et al., 2020; Weinshenker, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Morris et al., 2020 and Weinshenker, 2018.

claim: The LC is one of the earliest sites of degeneration in both Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD).
source: The LC is one of the earliest sites of degeneration in both Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), and profound loss of LC-NE neurons is evident with disease progression (Weinshenker, 2018; Mather and Harley, 2016; Chalermpalanupap et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Weinshenker, 2018; Mather and Harley, 2016; Chalermpalanupap et al., 2017.

claim: Profound loss of LC-NE neurons is evident with disease progression in Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease.
source: The LC is one of the earliest sites of degeneration in both Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), and profound loss of LC-NE neurons is evident with disease progression (Weinshenker, 2018; Mather and Harley, 2016; Chalermpalanupap et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Weinshenker, 2018; Mather and Harley, 2016; Chalermpalanupap et al., 2017.

claim: Maintaining the neural density of LC-NE neurons prevents cognitive decline during aging.
source: Moreover, maintaining the neural density of LC-NE neurons prevents cognitive decline during aging (Wilson et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wilson et al., 2013.

claim: Primary neuropathologies for AD (hyperphosphorylated tau) and PD (alpha-synuclein) can be detected in the LC prior to other brain regions.
source: In addition, primary neuropathologies for AD (hyperphosphorylated tau) and PD (alpha-synuclein) can be detected in the LC prior to other brain regions (Grudzien et al., 2007; Andrés-Benito et al., 2017; Braak and Del Tredici, 2012; Del Tredici and Braak, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Grudzien et al., 2007; Andrés-Benito et al., 2017; Braak and Del Tredici, 2012; Del Tredici and Braak, 2013.

claim: Noradrenergic signaling controls sustained attention, and its dysregulation is associated with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
source: Noradrenergic signaling controls many cognitive functions, including sustained attention, and its dysregulation is associated with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) (Asherson et al., 2016; Biederman and Spencer, 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Asherson et al., 2016; Biederman and Spencer, 1999.

claim: The NE reuptake inhibitor atomoxetine is the first non-stimulant medication that is FDA-approved for treating ADHD.
source: Related to these findings, the NE reuptake inhibitor atomoxetine is the first non-stimulant medication that is FDA-approved for treating ADHD (Bouret and Sara, 2004; Bymaster et al., 2002; Newman et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Bouret and Sara, 2004; Bymaster et al., 2002; Newman et al., 2008.

claim: Disruption of noradrenergic signaling is associated with anxiety, addiction, and responses to stress and trauma.
source: Disruption of noradrenergic signaling is also associated with anxiety, addiction, and responses to stress and trauma, and drugs that modulate noradrenergic signaling have been used in the treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), major depressive disorder (MDD), anxiety, and opioid withdrawal (Morris et al., 2020; Dell'Osso et al., 2011; Weinshenker and Schroeder, 2007; Berridge and Waterhouse, 2003; Urits et al., 2020; Paiva et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Morris et al., 2020; Dell'Osso et al., 2011; Weinshenker and Schroeder, 2007; Berridge and Waterhouse, 2003; Urits et al., 2020; Paiva et al., 2021.

claim: Drugs that modulate noradrenergic signaling have been used in the treatment of PTSD, MDD, anxiety, and opioid withdrawal.
source: Disruption of noradrenergic signaling is also associated with anxiety, addiction, and responses to stress and trauma, and drugs that modulate noradrenergic signaling have been used in the treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), major depressive disorder (MDD), anxiety, and opioid withdrawal (Morris et al., 2020; Dell'Osso et al., 2011; Weinshenker and Schroeder, 2007; Berridge and Waterhouse, 2003; Urits et al., 2020; Paiva et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Morris et al., 2020; Dell'Osso et al., 2011; Weinshenker and Schroeder, 2007; Berridge and Waterhouse, 2003; Urits et al., 2020; Paiva et al., 2021.

claim: This study used a combination of spatially-resolved transcriptomics and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing to characterize the molecular landscape of the LC region in the human brain.
source: Here, we used a combination of spatially-resolved transcriptomics and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing to characterize the molecular landscape of the LC region and the transcriptomic profile of LC-NE neurons in the human brain.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the methods used in the study.

claim: The study provides a freely accessible resource of the data in web-accessible and downloadable formats.
source: We provide a freely accessible resource of these data in web-accessible and downloadable formats.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the data availability.

claim: Five neurotypical adult human brain donors were selected to characterize transcriptome-wide gene expression within the LC.
source: We selected five neurotypical adult human brain donors to characterize transcriptome-wide gene expression within the LC at spatial and single-nucleus resolution using the 10x Genomics Visium SRT (10x Genomics, 2022a) and 10x Genomics Chromium snRNA-seq (10x Genomics, 2022b) platforms (see Supplementary file 1 for donor demographic details).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the study design.

claim: After all quality control (QC) steps, the final SRT dataset consisted of samples from 4 donors.
source: After all quality control (QC) steps (described below), the final SRT and snRNA-seq datasets used for analyses consisted of samples from 4 and 3 donors, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the final dataset.

claim: After all quality control (QC) steps, the final snRNA-seq dataset consisted of samples from 3 donors.
source: After all quality control (QC) steps (described below), the final SRT and snRNA-seq datasets used for analyses consisted of samples from 4 and 3 donors, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the final dataset.

claim: The LC was visually identified by neuroanatomical landmarks and the presence of the pigment neuromelanin on transverse slabs of the pons.
source: In each tissue sample, the LC was first visually identified by neuroanatomical landmarks and the presence of the pigment neuromelanin on transverse slabs of the pons (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the identification method, and Figure 1A provides visual evidence.

claim: Prior to SRT and snRNA-seq assays, the presence of NE neuron marker genes (TH and SLC6A2) was confirmed by multiplexed single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization (smFISH) using RNAscope.
source: Specifically, we cut 10 μm cryosections from tissue blocks from each donor and probed for the presence of a pan-neuronal marker gene (SNAP25) and two NE neuron-specific marker genes (TH and SLC6A2) by multiplexed single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization (smFISH) using RNAscope (Maynard et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2012; Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the validation method, and Figure 1B provides visual evidence.

claim: Robust mRNA signal from NE neuron marker genes was used as a quality control measure in all tissue blocks prior to proceeding with inclusion in the study.
source: Robust mRNA signal from these markers, visualized as puncta on imaged tissue sections, was used as a quality control measure in all tissue blocks prior to proceeding with inclusion in the study and performing SRT and snRNA-seq assays.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the quality control procedure.

claim: 10 μm tissue sections were used for gene expression profiling at spatial resolution using the 10x Genomics Visium SRT platform.
source: For tissue blocks included in the study, we cut additional 10 μm tissue sections, which were used for gene expression profiling at spatial resolution using the 10x Genomics Visium SRT platform (10x Genomics, 2022a; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the SRT method, and Figure 1C provides a schematic.

claim: Each Visium capture area contains approximately 5000 expression spots with diameter 55 μm and 100 μm center-to-center spacing.
source: Fresh-frozen tissue sections were placed onto each of four capture areas per Visium slide, where each capture area contains approximately 5000 expression spots (spatial measurement locations with diameter 55 μm and 100 μm center-to-center, where transcripts are captured) laid out in a honeycomb pattern.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the Visium platform specifications.

claim: Spatial barcodes unique to each spot are incorporated during reverse transcription, allowing the spatial coordinates of the gene expression measurements to be identified.
source: Spatial barcodes unique to each spot are incorporated during reverse transcription, thus allowing the spatial coordinates of the gene expression measurements to be identified (10x Genomics, 2022a).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the Visium platform technology.

claim: Tissue blocks were scored to fit 2–3 tissue sections from the same donor onto a single capture area to maximize the use of the Visium slides.
source: Given the small size of the LC compared to the area of the array, tissue blocks were scored to fit 2–3 tissue sections from the same donor onto a single capture area to maximize the use of the Visium slides, resulting in a total of n=9 Visium capture areas (hereafter referred to as samples).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the experimental design.

claim: A total of n=9 Visium capture areas (samples) were generated from the five brain donors.
source: Given the small size of the LC compared to the area of the array, tissue blocks were scored to fit 2–3 tissue sections from the same donor onto a single capture area to maximize the use of the Visium slides, resulting in a total of n=9 Visium capture areas (hereafter referred to as samples).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the final number of samples.

claim: For 3 of the 5 donors, 100 μm sections were cut from the same tissue blocks to profile transcriptome-wide gene expression at single-nucleus resolution with the 10x Genomics Chromium single cell 3' gene expression platform.
source: For 3 of the 5 donors, we cut additional 100 μm sections from the same tissue blocks to profile transcriptome-wide gene expression at single-nucleus resolution with the 10x Genomics Chromium single cell 3' gene expression platform (10x Genomics, 2022b; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the snRNA-seq method, and Figure 1C provides a schematic.

claim: Neuronal enrichment was employed with fluorescence-activated nuclear sorting (FANS) prior to library preparation to enhance the capture of neuronal population diversity.
source: Neuronal enrichment was employed with fluorescence-activated nuclear sorting (FANS) prior to library preparation to enhance the capture of neuronal population diversity, and snRNA-seq assays were subsequently completed.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the snRNA-seq method.

claim: Spots within regions identified as containing LC-NE neurons were manually annotated based on pigmentation, cell size, and morphology from the H&E stained histology images.
source: First, we manually annotated spots within regions identified as containing LC-NE neurons, based on pigmentation, cell size, and morphology from the H&E stained histology images (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the annotation method, and Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1 provide visual evidence.

claim: The median number of cells per spot within the LC regions ranged from 2 to 5 per sample.
source: Analysis of cell segmentations of the H&E images (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A) revealed that the median number of cells per spot within the LC regions ranged from 2 to 5 per sample (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the cell density analysis, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B provides visual evidence.

claim: One sample (Br5459_LC_round2) was excluded from subsequent analyses due to lack of clear expression of NE neuron marker genes (TH and SLC6A2).
source: Next, we performed additional sample-level QC on the initial n=9 Visium capture areas (hereafter referred to as samples) by visualizing the expression of two NE neuron-specific marker genes (TH and SLC6A2) (Figure 2B), which identified one sample (Br5459_LC_round2) without clear expression of these markers (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–B). This sample was excluded from subsequent analyses, leaving n=8 samples from 4 out of the 5 donors.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the quality control procedure, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–B provides visual evidence.

claim: For the n=8 Visium samples, the annotated regions were highly enriched in the expression of the NE neuron marker genes (TH and SLC6A2).
source: For the n=8 Visium samples, the annotated regions were highly enriched in the expression of the NE neuron marker genes (TH and SLC6A2) (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 3C), confirming that these samples captured dense regions of LC-NE neurons within the annotated regions.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the validation of the annotated regions, and Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 3C provide visual evidence.

claim: Spot-level QC was performed independently within each sample due to large differences in read depth between samples.
source: Due to the large differences in read depth between samples (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A, Supplementary file 1, Methods), we performed spot-level QC independently within each sample.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the quality control procedure, and Figure 2—figure supplement 4A provides visual evidence.

claim: After filtering low-expressed genes, the final dataset consisted of a total of 12,827 genes and 20,380 spots across the n=8 samples.
source: After filtering low-expressed genes (Methods), this resulted in a total of 12,827 genes and 20,380 spots across the n=8 samples used for downstream analyses (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the final dataset, and Figure 2—figure supplement 4B provides visual evidence.

claim: Differential expression (DE) testing between the pseudobulked manually annotated LC and non-LC regions identified 32 highly significant genes at a false discovery rate (FDR) threshold of 10–3 and expression fold-change (FC) threshold of 3.
source: This analysis identified 32 highly significant genes at a false discovery rate (FDR) threshold of 10–3 and expression FC threshold of 3 (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 8A).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the differential expression analysis results, and Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 8A provide visual evidence.

claim: The 32 highly significant genes identified by DE testing include known NE neuron marker genes DBH (top-ranked), SLC6A2 (ranked 6th), TH (ranked 7th), and SLC18A2 (ranked 14th).
source: This includes known NE neuron marker genes including DBH (the top-ranked gene by FDR within this set), SLC6A2 (ranked 6th), TH (ranked 7th), and SLC18A2 (ranked 14th).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the differential expression analysis results.

claim: Out of the 32 highly significant genes, 31 were elevated in expression within the LC regions, while one (MCM5) was depleted.
source: Out of the 32 genes, 31 were elevated in expression within the LC regions, while one (MCM5) was depleted.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the differential expression analysis results.

claim: The set of 32 highly significant genes includes one long noncoding RNA (LINC00682), while the remaining 31 genes are protein-coding genes.
source: The set includes one long noncoding RNA (LINC00682), while the remaining 31 genes are protein-coding genes (Figure 2E and Supplementary file 2A).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the differential expression analysis results, and Figure 2E provides visual evidence.

claim: Using standard significance thresholds of FDR <0.05 and expression FC >2, a total of 437 statistically significant genes were identified.
source: Alternatively, using standard significance thresholds of FDR <0.05 and expression FC >2, we identified a total of 437 statistically significant genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 8B and Supplementary file 2A).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the differential expression analysis results, and Figure 2—figure supplement 8B provides visual evidence.

claim: A small number of genes from rodent LC studies (Mulvey et al., 2018; Grimm et al., 2004) were highly associated with the manually annotated LC regions in the human data, including DBH, TH, and SLC6A2 from Mulvey et al., 2018, and DBH and GNAS from Grimm et al., 2004.
source: A small number of genes from both studies were highly associated with the manually annotated LC regions in the human data, including DBH, TH, and SLC6A2 from Mulvey et al., 2018, and DBH and GNAS from Grimm et al., 2004.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the cross-species comparison results.

claim: The majority of the genes from rodent LC studies (Mulvey et al., 2018; Grimm et al., 2004) were expressed at low levels in the human data.
source: However, the majority of the genes from both studies were expressed at low levels in the human data, which may reflect species-specific differences in the biological function of these genes as well as differences due to the experimental technologies employed (Figure 2F–G).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the cross-species comparison results, and Figure 2F–G provide visual evidence.

claim: After raw data processing, doublet removal, and standard QC and filtering, a total of 20,191 nuclei were obtained across the three snRNA-seq samples.
source: After raw data processing, doublet removal using scDblFinder (Germain et al., 2021), and standard QC and filtering, we obtained a total of 20,191 nuclei across the three samples (7957, 3015, and 9219 nuclei respectively from donors Br2701, Br6522, and Br8079) (see Supplementary file 1 for additional details).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the snRNA-seq data processing.

claim: An unexpectedly high proportion of mitochondrial reads was observed in nuclei with expression of NE neuron marker genes (DBH, TH, and SLC6A2).
source: We observed an unexpectedly high proportion of mitochondrial reads in nuclei with expression of NE neuron marker genes (DBH, TH, and SLC6A2), which represented our rare population of interest, and hence we did not remove nuclei based on the proportion of mitochondrial reads (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and Figure 3—figure supplement 3, additional details described below).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the quality control observations, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and Figure 3—figure supplement 3 provide visual evidence.

claim: The unsupervised clustering workflow identified 30 clusters, including clusters representing major neuronal and non-neuronal cell populations.
source: The unsupervised clustering workflow identified 30 clusters, including clusters representing major neuronal and non-neuronal cell populations, which we labeled based on the expression of known marker genes (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the clustering results, and Figure 3A–B provide visual evidence.

claim: A cluster of NE neurons consisting of 295 nuclei (168, 4, and 123 nuclei from donors Br2701, Br6522, and Br8079, respectively) was identified based on the expression of NE neuron marker genes (DBH, TH, and SLC6A2).
source: This included a cluster of NE neurons consisting of 295 nuclei (168, 4, and 123 nuclei from donors Br2701, Br6522, and Br8079, respectively), which we identified based on the expression of NE neuron marker genes (DBH, TH, and SLC6A2).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the NE neuron cluster identification.

claim: In addition to the NE neuron cluster, clusters representing excitatory neurons, inhibitory neurons, astrocytes, endothelial and mural cells, macrophages and microglia, oligodendrocytes, and oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) were identified.
source: In addition to the NE neuron cluster, we identified clusters representing excitatory neurons, inhibitory neurons, astrocytes, endothelial and mural cells, macrophages and microglia, oligodendrocytes, and oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs), as well as several clusters with ambiguous expression profiles including pan-neuronal marker genes (SNAP25 and SYT1) without clear expression of excitatory or inhibitory neuronal markers, which may represent damaged neuronal nuclei and debris (Figure 3A–B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the clustering results, and Figure 3A–B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1 provide visual evidence.

claim: Standard QC metrics (sum of UMI counts and detected genes) for the NE neuron cluster fell within the ranges of values observed for the other neuronal and non-neuronal clusters.
source: Further evaluation of QC metrics revealed that standard QC metrics (sum of UMI counts and detected genes) for the NE neuron cluster fell within the ranges of values observed for the other neuronal and non-neuronal clusters (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B), and that the ambiguous neuronal category included a clear subset of measurements with the overall highest mitochondrial proportions and lowest number of detected genes (likely damaged nuclei and/or debris), which remained separate from the NE neuron cluster (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C, D), thus providing additional confidence that the high mitochondrial proportions observed for the NE neuron cluster were not due to mis-classified damaged nuclei and/or debris.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the quality control evaluation, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B, C, D provide visual evidence.

claim: The 327 statistically significant genes with elevated expression in the NE neuron cluster include known NE neuron marker genes (DBH, TH, SLC6A2, and SLC18A2) as well as the 13 protein-coding mitochondrial genes.
source: These genes include known NE neuron marker genes (DBH, TH, SLC6A2, and SLC18A2) as well as the 13 protein-coding mitochondrial genes, which are highly expressed in large, metabolically active NE neurons (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 5A, and Supplementary file 2C).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the differential expression analysis results, and Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 5A provide visual evidence.

claim: DE testing between the NE neuron cluster and all other clusters (neuronal and non-neuronal, excluding ambiguous) in the snRNA-seq data identified 427 statistically significant genes with elevated expression in the NE neuron cluster at an FDR threshold of 0.05 and FC threshold of 2.
source: To compare with the spatial data, we also performed DE testing between the NE neuron cluster and all other clusters (neuronal and non-neuronal, excluding ambiguous) in the snRNA-seq data, which identified 427 statistically significant genes with elevated expression in the NE neuron cluster at an FDR threshold of 0.05 and FC threshold of 2, including all of the 327 genes above (Figure 3—figure supplement 6 and Supplementary file 2D).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the differential expression analysis results, and Figure 3—figure supplement 6 provides visual evidence.

claim: Comparison of the 427 statistically significant DE genes from the snRNA-seq data with the 437 statistically significant DE genes from the SRT data generated a list of 51 genes that were identified as statistically significant DE genes in both datasets.
source: We then compared these genes with the set of 437 statistically significant DE genes from the pseudobulked analyses (LC vs. non-LC regions) in the SRT data, which generated a list of 51 genes that were identified as statistically significant DE genes in both the SRT and snRNA-seq datasets.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the comparison results.

claim: The 51 genes identified as statistically significant DE genes in both the SRT and snRNA-seq datasets included known NE neuron marker genes (DBH, TH, SLC6A2, and SLC18A2) with high FC in both datasets.
source: These 51 genes included known NE neuron marker genes (DBH, TH, SLC6A2, and SLC18A2) with high FC in both datasets (Figure 3—figure supplement 7 and Supplementary file 2E).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the comparison results, and Figure 3—figure supplement 7 provides visual evidence.

claim: Several genes from rodent LC studies (Mulvey et al., 2018; Grimm et al., 2004) were conserved across species in the human snRNA-seq data.
source: Consistent with the SRT samples, we observed that several genes were conserved across species.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the cross-species comparison results.

claim: Compared to the SRT samples, relatively higher expression of the conserved genes was observed within the NE neuron cluster in the snRNA-seq data.
source: However, compared to the SRT samples, we observed relatively higher expression of the conserved genes within the NE neuron cluster, which is expected since the NE neuron cluster contains reads from individual nuclei from this population only, while the SRT data may contain reads from nuclei, cytoplasm, and cell processes from up to multiple cell populations per spot.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the cross-species comparison results.

claim: A cluster of potential 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT, serotonin) neurons was identified in the unsupervised clustering analyses of the snRNA-seq data based on the expression of 5-HT neuron marker genes (TPH2 and SLC6A4).
source: In addition to NE neurons, we identified a cluster of potential 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT, serotonin) neurons in the unsupervised clustering analyses of the snRNA-seq data (Figure 3A–B) based on the expression of 5-HT neuron marker genes (TPH2 and SLC6A4) (Ren et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the 5-HT neuron cluster identification, and Figure 3A–B provide visual evidence.

claim: The 5-HT neuron cluster consisted of 186 nuclei (145, 28, and 13 nuclei from donors Br2701, Br6522, and Br8079, respectively).
source: This cluster consisted of 186 nuclei (145, 28, and 13 nuclei from donors Br2701, Br6522, and Br8079, respectively).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the 5-HT neuron cluster.

claim: DE testing between the neuronal clusters identified 361 statistically significant genes with elevated expression in the 5-HT neuron cluster, compared to all other neuronal clusters, at an FDR threshold of 0.05 and FC threshold of 2.
source: DE testing between the neuronal clusters identified 361 statistically significant genes with elevated expression in the 5-HT neuron cluster, compared to all other neuronal clusters captured in this region, at an FDR threshold of 0.05 and FC threshold of 2.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the differential expression analysis results.

claim: The 361 statistically significant genes with elevated expression in the 5-HT neuron cluster included the 5-HT neuron marker genes TPH2 and SLC6A4.
source: These genes included the 5-HT neuron marker genes TPH2 and SLC6A4 (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 5B, and Supplementary file 2F).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the differential expression analysis results, and Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 5B provide visual evidence.

claim: The 5-HT neuron population was distributed across both the LC and non-LC regions in the Visium samples.
source: To investigate the spatial distribution of this population, we visualized the spatial expression of the 5-HT neuron marker genes TPH2 and SLC6A4 in the n=9 initial Visium samples, which showed that this population was distributed across both the LC and non-LC regions (Figure 3—figure supplement 9A, B).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the spatial distribution analysis, and Figure 3—figure supplement 9A, B provide visual evidence.

claim: No significant spatial enrichment of TPH2 and SLC6A4 expression was observed within the manually annotated LC regions in the n=8 Visium samples that passed QC.
source: Similarly, we did not observe significant spatial enrichment of TPH2 and SLC6A4 expression within the manually annotated LC regions in the n=8 Visium samples that passed QC (Figure 3—figure supplement 9C).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the spatial distribution analysis, and Figure 3—figure supplement 9C provides visual evidence.

claim: RNAscope applied to additional tissue sections from donor Br6522 demonstrated that the NE and 5-HT marker genes were expressed within distinct cells and these neuronal populations were not localized within the same regions.
source: To further confirm this finding, we applied RNAscope (Wang et al., 2012) to visualize expression of an NE neuron marker gene (TH) and 5-HT neuron marker genes (TPH2 and SLC6A4) within additional tissue sections from donor Br6522, which demonstrated that the NE and 5-HT marker genes were expressed within distinct cells and these neuronal populations were not localized within the same regions (Figure 3—figure supplement 11), and the 5-HT neuron marker genes (TPH2 and SLC6A4) were co-expressed within individual cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 12).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the RNAscope validation, and Figure 3—figure supplement 11 and Figure 3—figure supplement 12 provide visual evidence.

claim: The 5-HT neuron marker genes (TPH2 and SLC6A4) were co-expressed within individual cells.
source: To further confirm this finding, we applied RNAscope (Wang et al., 2012) to visualize expression of an NE neuron marker gene (TH) and 5-HT neuron marker genes (TPH2 and SLC6A4) within additional tissue sections from donor Br6522, which demonstrated that the NE and 5-HT marker genes were expressed within distinct cells and these neuronal populations were not localized within the same regions (Figure 3—figure supplement 11), and the 5-HT neuron marker genes (TPH2 and SLC6A4) were co-expressed within individual cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 12).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the RNAscope validation, and Figure 3—figure supplement 12 provides visual evidence.

claim: A secondary round of unsupervised clustering applied to the inhibitory neuron nuclei identified 14 clusters representing inhibitory neuronal subpopulations.
source: We also investigated the diversity of inhibitory neuronal subpopulations within the snRNA-seq data from the human LC and the surrounding region by applying a secondary round of unsupervised clustering to the inhibitory neuron nuclei identified in the first round of clustering. This identified 14 clusters representing inhibitory neuronal subpopulations, which varied in their expression of several inhibitory neuronal marker genes including CALB1, CALB2, TAC1, CNR1, and VIP (additional marker genes shown in Figure 3—figure supplements 8 and 13A).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the manuscript describing the secondary clustering results, and Figure 3—figure supplements 8 and 13A provide visual evidence.
